title: Dead to Sin, Alive to God, Slaves to Righteousness

questions.question: Paul asks: "Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound?" What is his immediate response to this?
options: By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?
Only if we confess our sins daily, for he is faithful and just.
We cannot, for sin has no more power in the world.
God forbid! For the law still commands our obedience.
questions.correctAnswer: By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:1-2 (ESV): "What shall we say then? Are we to continue in sin that grace may abound? By no means! How can we who died to sin still live in it?"

questions.question: Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into what?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:3 (ESV): "Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?"

questions.question: We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in what?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:4 (ESV): "We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life."

questions.question: For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in what?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:5 (ESV): "For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we shall certainly be united with him in a resurrection like his."

questions.question: We know that our old self was crucified with him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we would no longer be what?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:6 (ESV): "We know that our old self was crucified with him in order that the body of sin might be brought to nothing, so that we would no longer be enslaved to sin."

questions.question: For one who has died has been set free from what?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:7 (ESV): "For one who has died has been set free from sin."

questions.question: We know that Christ, being raised from the dead, will never die again. What no longer has dominion over him?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:9 (ESV): "We know that Christ, being raised from the dead, will never die again; death no longer has dominion over him."

questions.question: For the death he died he died to sin, once for all, but the life he lives he lives to whom?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:10 (ESV): "For the death he died he died to sin, once for all, but the life he lives he lives to God."

questions.question: So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in whom?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:11 (ESV): "So you also must consider yourselves dead to sin and alive to God in Christ Jesus."

questions.question: Do not present your members to sin as instruments for unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and your members to God as what?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:13 (ESV): "Do not present your members to sin as instruments for unrighteousness, but present yourselves to God as those who have been brought from death to life, and your members to God as instruments for righteousness."

questions.question: Why will sin have no dominion over you?
options: Since you are not under law but under grace
Because the Holy Spirit dwells within you
For you have been bought with a price
Because the blood of Christ cleanses from all sin
questions.correctAnswer: Since you are not under law but under grace
questions.explanation: Romans 6:14 (ESV): "For sin will have no dominion over you, since you are not under law but under grace."

questions.question: If you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to what?
questions.explanation: Romans 6:16 (ESV): "Do you not know that if you present yourselves to anyone as obedient slaves, you are slaves of the one whom you obey, either of sin, which leads to death, or of obedience, which leads to righteousness?"

questions.question: But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to what?
options: The standard of teaching to which you were committed
The law of liberty in Christ Jesus
The Spirit of truth who guides you
questions.correctAnswer: The standard of teaching to which you were committed
questions.explanation: Romans 6:17 (ESV): "But thanks be to God, that you who were once slaves of sin have become obedient from the heart to the standard of teaching to which you were committed,"

questions.question: Now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, what is the fruit you get?
options: It leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life
It brings joy unspeakable and full of glory
It results in peace that passes all understanding
It produces love, joy, peace, patience, and kindness
questions.correctAnswer: It leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life
questions.explanation: Romans 6:22 (ESV): "But now that you have been set free from sin and have become slaves of God, the fruit you get leads to sanctification and its end, eternal life."

questions.question: What are the wages of sin, and what is the free gift of God?
options: The wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord
The wages of sin is sorrow, but the free gift is joy in the Holy Spirit
The wages of sin is hell, but the free gift is heaven through faith
The wages of sin is separation, but the free gift is reconciliation
questions.correctAnswer: The wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord
questions.explanation: Romans 6:23 (ESV): "For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord."

key_verse_text: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.
